question: Random variable $X$ has the following distribution: $P(X=0) = p, P(X=1) = 2p, P(X=2) = 3p, P(X=3) = 4p$. Find $p$, and hence compute $P(X>1)$.
explanation:
Sum of probabilities = 1:
$p + 2p + 3p + 4p = 1$
$10p = 1$
$p = 0.1$

$P(X > 1) = P(X=2) + P(X=3) = 3p + 4p = 7p = 7 \times 0.1 = 0.7$

Final answers: $p=0.1$, $P(X>1) = 0.7$.
